(a) The probability is \int_0^1\int_{1/6}^1 {2 \over 3} (x + 2y) \,dx\,dy = \int_0^1 {2\over3} ({1\over2}x^2 + 2xy)\bigr|^1_{1/6}\,dy = \int_0^1 {2\over3} \left[({1\over2} + 2y) - ({1\over 72} + {\frac{1}{3}}y)\right]\,dy = {2\over3}\int_0^1 (\frac{35}{72} + \frac{5}{3} y) \, dy = {2\over3} \left(\frac{35}{72} y + \frac{5}{6} y^2\right)\bigr|_0^1 = {2\over3} \left(\frac{95}{72}\right) = \frac{95}{108}.
(b) It is easier to calculate the probability that x \lt \frac1{6} + y does not happen, that is, the probability that x \ge \frac1{6} + y, and subtract it from 1. The probability that x \ge \frac1{6} + y is \int_{0}^{5/6}\int_{y+1/6}^{1} {2\over3} (x+2y) \,dx\,dy = \int_{0}^{5/6} (\frac13\,x^2 + \frac43\,xy) \bigr|_{y+(1/6)}^{1} \,dy = \int_{0}^{5/6} \frac13\left(1 - (\frac1{6} + y)^2\right) + \frac43(y)(1 - (\frac1{6} + y)) \,dy = \int_{0}^{5/6} -\frac53\,y^2 + y + \frac{35}{108} \, dy = (-\frac59\,y^3 + \frac{1}{2}\, y^2 + \frac{35}{108}\,y)\bigr|_{0}^{5/6} = \frac{575}{1944}. Thus, the probability that x \lt \frac1{6}+y is 1-(\frac{575}{1944}) = \frac{1369}{1944}.
